subject: Dedicated capacity: footprint & telemetry questionnaire
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah@lumina.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Jul 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: footprint & telemetry questionnaire

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday — excited to help Lumina scope a Dedicated fleet that keeps your latency targets within budget. To speed up sizing, attached is a short CSV template (traffic_sample_template.csv) that captures the inputs our sizing engine needs. Can you fill or export the closest equivalent from your telemetry team and return it? Key items we need in the sample: 

- For each API route (inference / chat / embeddings): average and P95 tokens-per-call (prompt + response)
- Typical prompt length distribution (25th/50th/75th percentiles) and max prompt size
- Average response length and max response size
- Session semantics: are you using long-lived sessions with persistent KV caches? If so, approximate session length (minutes/hours) and KV cache hit-rate estimate
- Concurrent sessions vs concurrent requests (do sessions multiplex requests?)
- Peak QPS and the 1-hour sustained peak vs 1-week peak day
- Typical model(s) you plan to serve and whether you’ll accept quantized variants
- Region preference (you mentioned EU), and any data residency / retention constraints
- Any hard latency SLOs (P95 token latency target or P99 end-to-end) and acceptable degradation/fallback behavior

If you don’t have full traces, a representative 24–72 hour CSV export or even a randomized sample (1%) helps a lot. Once we have that we’ll run a rapid sizing pass and share a preliminary GPU mix + oversubscription plan.

Next steps: if you can return the filled CSV by Monday (21 Jul) we’ll aim to deliver an initial sizing and a short readout the same week. If it helps, happy to do a 30-min walkthrough with your telemetry engineer.

Thanks,

--
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com

Attachment: traffic_sample_template.csv (CSV stub: route, timestamp, avg_prompt_tokens, avg_response_tokens, sample_session_id, session_length_seconds, kv_cache_hit_rate, region)

From: Sarah Liu <sarah@lumina.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@lumina.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 08:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: footprint & telemetry questionnaire

Hi Camila — thanks, attached is a quick export (lumina_traffic_sample.csv). A few notes up front: 

- Region: EU (we need data residency inside eu-west-1)
- Models: 1x opt-13b-finetuned (production), 1x 7b for internal dev; we can accept int8 quantization for the 7b in non-prod
- Average prompt length: 120 tokens (median 95, 75th 180), max prompt ~3,200 tokens
- Average response length: 85 tokens, max response 1,024
- Sessions: we do long-lived sessions for chat (avg session ~2h), KV cache hit-rate ~88% per session after warm-up. Sessions do multiplex — 1 session may generate multiple outgoing requests over time
- Peak: observed 420 qps sustained for 6 minutes during a marketing push; 1-hour sustained peak around 180 qps; typical daily median ~22 qps
- Latency: product asks for P95 end-to-end < 350 ms for small completions (<200 tokens); we can accept fallback to a lower-cost variant during sustained overloads

I don’t have P99 numbers in this export; if you need them I can pull extended traces but it will be a day or two.

Attaching lumina_traffic_sample.csv for the fields you requested. Happy to hop on a short call — suggest Wednesday 16:00 CEST.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Liu
Head of Infrastructure | Lumina Labs
sarah@lumina.ai

Attachment: lumina_traffic_sample.csv (CSV stub: sample rows included, anonymized session ids)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Liu <sarah@lumina.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: footprint & telemetry questionnaire

Thanks for the export, Sarah — good signal in there. Quick internal take:

- With a session average of ~2h and KV hit-rate ~88%, we can rely on heavy KV caching to reduce token compute for warmed sessions. That implies fewer GPUs required for steady traffic than raw QPS would suggest, but we still need headroom for cold-start bursts.
- The 420 qps 6-minute spike is the main sizing driver; model choices (13b production) push us toward 2x A10x or mixed A100 + A10k SKUs depending on desired P95 latency and oversubscription.

Clarifying questions for the runbook before we size:
1) For the 13b path, are you open to a small quality delta (int8) during 2–3% of traffic in exchange for 30–40% lower GPU hours during sustained peaks?
2) Do you use streaming partial responses to the client or do you buffer full completions server-side? (affects commit-to-send token compute and latency windows)
3) Any expected growth cadence in the next 3 months (e.g., marketing campaigns) beyond the 420 qps spike?

I sketched a prelim fleet view (prelim-fleet-sketch.png) that shows a 3-stage staging->canary->prod deployment with canary size ~10% of prod and automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant in a different region if EU capacity is constrained. Will attach to the readout notes.

If Camila and Karthik agree, I’ll run two quick scenarios: conservative (no quantization, higher GPU count) and cost-optimized (selective int8 for non-critical routes + autoscale thresholds).

-Marissa

Attachment: prelim-fleet-sketch.png (PNG stub: fleet blocks, expected GPU counts per node type, autoscale triggers)

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah@lumina.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: footprint & telemetry questionnaire

Perfect, thanks everyone — this is actionable. A couple of quick items: 

- Sarah: Wednesday 16:00 CEST works for the call; I’ll send a calendar invite with a short agenda (30 min: sizing readout + next steps).
- Marissa: please run the two scenarios you outlined and include a brief note on expected P95 tail behavior (with and without selective int8) and estimated monthly committed GPU hours for each plan. Karthik, can you add a short note on recommended oversubscription ratios for session-heavy workloads (given Lumina’s multiplexing behavior)?
- Sarah: we’ll mark the EU region requirement in the proposal; if procurement needs an initial statement of work we can attach an early draft (I’ll draft after the readout).

Next steps: 1) Marissa/Karthik produce the two-scenario sizing sheet and send by EOD Thursday (24 Jul) 2) 30-min readout Wed 16:00 CEST 3) Proposal draft by next Tuesday.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

--
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com
